config.title: Form Library from Scratch

intro.title: Form Library from Scratch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form library from scratch using React and JavaScript. You will learn how to create reusable form components that manage their own state and validation. The core programming concepts involved include React hooks for state management and event handling. You will work with JSX to structure your forms and handlers to process user input. By the end, you'll have a basic custom form library that can handle text inputs and submissions. This project will help you understand how form libraries work under the hood.
intro.usecase: Form libraries like Formik and React Hook Form are essential in modern web applications where user input is critical. You'll encounter them in e-commerce checkout flows, user registration forms, admin dashboards for data entry, and settings panels where validation and state management are required. As a developer, you'll need to understand these patterns when building interactive features like multi-step wizards, dynamic form fields, or complex validation logic that goes beyond basic HTML forms. Mastering form library concepts helps you create maintainable, reusable form components that handle user input reliably across your application.

objectives: Construct a custom React hook to manage form state and validation
Implement reusable form components with controlled input binding
Apply validation rules to form fields and display error messages
Configure form submission handlers with proper state management
Integrate form components with external state management patterns
Manipulate form data structures for submission and reset operations
Initialize form libraries with default values and configuration options

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, making React and useState available for use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main Form component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Form that accepts children as props and returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called Form that takes props as its parameter and returns null. You can use either function declaration or arrow function syntax.

seedCode.App.jsx:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the Form component here

steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a Form component defined that accepts children props.
successCriteria: Form component is defined as a function that takes props and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined a function named Form that accepts props and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Form component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named Form that takes props and returns null.

steps.title: Initialize form state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside the Form component, use useState to create a state variable called formValues initialized as an empty object.
steps.hint: Call useState with an empty object {} as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into formValues and setFormValues.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state with an object
const [user, setUser] = useState({ name: '', email: '' });
steps.expectedOutcome: The Form component will have a formValues state variable initialized as an empty object, ready to store form field values.
successCriteria: formValues state is declared using useState with an empty object initial value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using useState with an empty object {} as the initial value and naming the variable formValues.
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the Form component, use useState to create a state variable called formValues initialized as an empty object {}.

steps.title: Create the handleChange function
steps.instruction: Inside the Form component, create a function called handleChange that takes an event parameter and updates the formValues state with the input's name and value.
steps.hint: The function should use setFormValues to update the state. Access the input's name via event.target.name and its value via event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleChange function is defined inside the Form component and properly updates the formValues state when called with an input change event.
successCriteria: A handleChange function exists that takes an event parameter and updates formValues using setFormValues with the input's name and value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your handleChange function properly updates the formValues state using setFormValues with the input's name and value from the event.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleChange function isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a function that takes an event parameter and updates the formValues state using setFormValues.

steps.title: Create the handleSubmit function
steps.instruction: Inside your Form component, create a function named handleSubmit that takes an event parameter, prevents the default form submission, and logs the current formValues to the console.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts an event parameter, calls event.preventDefault(), and then logs formValues.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleSubmit function is defined, preventing default form submission and logging the form values.
successCriteria: A function named handleSubmit is defined, it takes an event parameter, calls event.preventDefault(), and logs formValues.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the handleSubmit function. Make sure it takes an event parameter, prevents default submission, and logs formValues.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleSubmit function is not yet correctly defined. It should accept an event, prevent default, and log the form values.

steps.title: Return the form structure with context provider
steps.instruction: In your Form component's return statement, replace the current return value with a form element that has an onSubmit handler set to handleSubmit. Inside the form, create a simple context provider object that passes formValues and handleChange to children.
steps.hint: Return a <form> element with onSubmit={handleSubmit}. Inside it, you can create a simple object like { formValues, handleChange } and pass it to children via React context or props. For now, just create the object and leave a comment about passing it down.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Form component now returns a form element with an onSubmit handler, and inside it, a context provider object is prepared to pass formValues and handleChange to children.
successCriteria: A context provider object with formValues and handleChange is created inside the form
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have the form element with onSubmit and the context provider object inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction: you need to return a form element with onSubmit={handleSubmit} and create a context provider object inside it.

steps.title: Create the Input component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Input that accepts name, type, and placeholder props. Return a simple input element with those props.
steps.hint: Define the Input component with props as parameters. Use destructuring to extract name, type, and placeholder from props. Return an input element with those attributes.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a reusable Input component that can be used inside forms with customizable name, type, and placeholder.
successCriteria: The Input component is defined as a function that accepts name, type, and placeholder props and returns an input element with those attributes.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your Input component accepts name, type, and placeholder props and returns an input element with those attributes.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Input component should be a function that takes name, type, and placeholder props and returns an input element with those props.

steps.title: Access form context in Input component
steps.instruction: Inside the Input component, access the form context to get formValues and handleChange.
steps.hint: You'll need to use the useContext hook to access the form context values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Input component will have access to formValues and handleChange from the form context.
successCriteria: The Input component uses useContext to access formValues and handleChange from the form context.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're accessing both formValues and handleChange from the context.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Input component doesn't properly access the form context. Try using useContext to get formValues and handleChange.

steps.title: Return input element with wired handlers
steps.instruction: In the Input component, return an input element with its value set from formValues, its onChange wired to handleChange, and its other props passed through.
steps.hint: Use the form context to access formValues and handleChange, then set the input's value and onChange attributes accordingly.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Input component now returns a controlled input element that uses formValues for its value and handleChange for its onChange event.
successCriteria: The Input component returns an input element with value and onChange attributes set, and passes through other props.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the input element has both value and onChange attributes set correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Input component should return an input element with value and onChange attributes. Review how to create controlled inputs in React.

steps.title: Create the SubmitButton component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named SubmitButton that accepts children as props.
steps.hint: Define a component that takes props as its parameter and returns a button element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A SubmitButton component is defined and ready to be used within the form.
successCriteria: The SubmitButton component is a functional component that accepts children as props and returns a button element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it accepts children as props and returns a button element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The SubmitButton component is not correctly defined. Ensure it's a functional component that accepts children as props and returns a button element.

steps.title: Return button with form context
steps.instruction: Inside the SubmitButton component, return a button element with type='submit' and children as its content.
steps.hint: The button should be a standard HTML button element with the submit type attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: The SubmitButton component will render a submit button element.
successCriteria: The SubmitButton component returns a button element with type='submit'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a button element with type='submit' inside the SubmitButton component.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. The SubmitButton component should return a button element with type='submit'.

steps.title: Export the Form, Input, and SubmitButton components
steps.instruction: Export the Form, Input, and SubmitButton components as named exports so they can be used in other files.
steps.hint: Use the export keyword before each component declaration or add export statements at the end of the file.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Form, Input, and SubmitButton components are exported and ready to be imported in other files.
successCriteria: Form, Input, and SubmitButton are exported as named exports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've exported some components, but make sure to export all three: Form, Input, and SubmitButton.
steps.feedbackWrong: The components are not properly exported. Check that you're using the export keyword for each component.
